newsitem.title: INDIA: India's RBI props up rupee at 35.70/71 vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: India's RBI props up rupee at 35.70/71 vs dollar.

text.p: The inter-bank forex market forced an early intervention by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Wednesday to prevent the rupee from breaching the 35.70-mark, dealers said.
"They must have bought $50-$60 million," said a chief dealer describing the size of the RBI's Wednesday afternoon purchases.
After two days of late evening strikes, the market was keen on forcing an early intervention by RBI on Wednesday.
On Monday and Tuesday, RBI stepped in only after the rupee breached the 35.70-mark. On Wednesday, it pre-empted the crash on time "maybe looking at the market's mood", a dealer said.
The latest quotes are at 35.707/712 rupees to a dollar.
"The bogeyman not only lurketh but he striketh as well," a European bank said in a forex commentary about RBI's 'enquiries' followed up by dollar purchases on Monday and Tuesday.
On Monday, the RBI bought up to 35.73, and on Tuesday up to the 35.71-level, dealers said.
